proves.claim: the search cell builds a TF-IDF index over item title, criterion and brief from the board.

search.index.builds-tfidf.why: Search quality depends on indexing all three fields.

proves.claim: deleting the sidecar and rebuilding from the board gives the same ranking.

search.index.rebuild-same-ranking.why: The sidecar is a cache, so losing it must change nothing.

proves.claim: only the search and add commands import the search cell.

search.index.only-search-and-add-import.why: Other callers would couple the cell to commands it should not serve.

proves.claim: the fixture holds the texts of every labelled item, so the test never reads the live board.

search.recall.fixture-holds-texts.why: A live-board read would make the recall figure drift.

proves.claim: at least 12 of the 13 reworded duplicates rank in the top 3.

search.recall.reworded-top3.why: Reworded duplicates are the case plain matching misses.

proves.claim: all 16 near-verbatim refiles rank in the top 3.

search.recall.refiles-top3.why: Near-verbatim refiles must never be missed.

proves.claim: every search-cell test has a stable ID and one complete record, and an unregistered test is reported and fails only with tests.registryStrict on.

search.registry.complete.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: Every search test file that reads files carries an input header naming what it reads.

search.inputs.every-reader-declares-its-.why: Affected-test selection can only see the inputs a test declares.

proves.claim: Every search input header names a cell, the test tree, the source tree or named files.

search.inputs.a-header-names-a-cell-neve.why: A malformed or whole-tree header would hide what a test really reads.

proves.claim: Only the listed whole-tree reader uses a tree header, and it still declares it.

search.inputs.only-the-listed-reader-use.why: A tree header makes a test rerun on every change, so it stays rare and listed.
